# ADR-0019: Vexel native project container v1

- Status: accepted for the codec foundation
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Decision owner: project owner
- Related: ADR-0018

## Decision

Vexel's native project is a single versioned `.vexel` file. Version 1 is a
bounded little-endian container holding a JSON metadata payload, exact SVG scene
source, a JSON timeline payload, and named raw assets. Keeping SVG source as an
opaque exact payload preserves Inkscape metadata and unrecognized constructs;
the native timeline can evolve independently of SVG animation interchange.

The fixed 56-byte header contains magic bytes `56 45 58 45 4c 0d 0a 1a`, version,
header size, metadata length, asset count, scene and timeline lengths, three
CRC-32/IEEE checksums, and zero flags. It is followed by metadata, scene,
timeline, then asset records. Each record has name/media-type lengths, a CRC-32
checksum over all three payload fields, a data length, and the exact name, media
type, and data bytes. All integers are little-endian. The full field table and limits live in
`src/project/README.md`.

Initial limits bound metadata to 1 MiB, scene to 256 MiB, timeline to 64 MiB,
assets to 1024 entries and 512 MiB aggregate, each asset to 256 MiB, and the
entire encoded project to 1 GiB. Asset names are unique safe single path
components. Decoders reject unknown versions/flags, checksum mismatches,
truncation, trailing data, duplicate names, unsafe names, and over-limit sizes.
The codec borrows input bytes and writes to caller-provided buffers; it does not
allocate or perform file I/O.

## Compatibility and limitations

Version 1's payloads are opaque to the container. Callers validate metadata and
timeline JSON and the scene SVG before use. A change to header layout, field
meaning, or incompatible payload semantics requires a new format version and an
explicit migration path; never silently reinterpret an unknown version. Future
work must wire file open/save, editor dirty state, atomic replacement, asset
import, compatibility UI, and recovery before claiming native project support.

CRC-32 detects accidental corruption but is not cryptographic authentication.
This format does not fetch resources or execute content. Asset names are
identifiers and are never extracted as paths by the codec.

## Rationale

A self-contained binary container supports bounded sequential I/O and avoids a
new archive dependency or path traversal during extraction. Raw sections keep
the codec independent from SVG and animation parsers and preserve bytes exactly.
The limits accommodate the project's large-document target while keeping
explicit ceilings. Apple document-package conventions remain useful for future
UX, but the chosen initial format is one file for straightforward sharing,
atomic save, and backup.
# ADR-0021: Native project recovery capsules

- Status: accepted for incremental implementation
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Decision owner: project owner
- Related: ADR-0018, ADR-0019

## Decision

Crash recovery for native projects stores a complete, independently validated
snapshot in a recovery capsule. A capsule records the originating document path,
the saved file's size and modification timestamp at the time edits began, the
capture time, and the complete encoded `.vexel` snapshot. It never replaces or
modifies the source project.

The project layer provides a bounded capsule codec and atomic file publication.
The application integration stores capsules in a private per-user Application
Support recovery directory, keyed by a digest of the standardized source path.
A capsule also contains the full path and must match it when opened; a key
collision or path mismatch is rejected. A later application work order wires
periodic background snapshots, retention, and recovery discovery to this API.

On restart, recovery is an explicit user choice. Vexel validates the capsule and
compares its saved baseline with the current source file. A matching baseline
can be restored as unsaved work. A changed or missing source is reported as a
recovery conflict; Vexel must not silently overwrite it. A successful normal
save or explicit discard removes the capsule. Atomic publication ensures a
crash during snapshot writing leaves either the previous complete capsule or
the newly published complete capsule.

CRC checks detect accidental corruption; they do not authenticate capsules.
Recovery remains local to the current macOS user account. It is not a backup or
synchronization service. Existing `.vexel` v1 content remains unchanged; the
capsule is a separate envelope and unknown project versions remain rejected.

## Consequences

Recovery snapshots contain the full project, including scene, native timeline,
metadata, and assets. The application must bound snapshot frequency and storage,
write off the UI thread, and make failures visible without blocking normal edits.
The per-user directory must be created with owner-only access. In-progress
application wiring and user interaction are not implied by the codec alone.

item.text:
**REJECT.** In [file.rs](/Users/megasoft78/Desktop/Freelance/vexel/.worktrees/rust4-project-io/rust/crates/vexel-project-io/src/file.rs:108), `project_file_save_encoded_with_hooks` maps every bundle decode error except `Limit` to `FileError::InvalidArgument`. The Rust decoder can return `project::Error::OutOfMemory` when its asset-name table allocation fails; the file API then reports invalid input even though `FileError::OutOfMemory` exists. Preserve that error class and add a focused regression proving the mapping.

The inspected recovery code matches the C capsule’s 72-byte layout, little-endian fields, CRC coverage, reserved-byte and nanosecond checks, validation precedence, borrowed views, and bundle error offsets. Save paths validate encoded bundles before publication, use the accepted atomic helpers, preserve publication/durability state, and keep recovery separate from the source. The hooks gate native operations and cannot report successful sync or publication themselves. Scoped Rust sources are under 800 lines, forbid unsafe code, and add no dependencies.

**Nonblocking coverage gaps:** No focused test covers encoded-save bundle checksum corruption before filesystem access; race coverage exercises new-file collision but not replacement races; recovery tests do not inject precommit file-sync or write failures. These gaps do not change the blocking error-mapping finding.

This was a read-only review; I did not run tests or builds. No full-app or live MCP certification was performed.
